messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i pull the fastener and check its position. it feels slightly loose, but the reading stays fine. i photograph the loose bolt and check whether the fastener catches. sorry—sorry, i’m putting it back. i’ll photograph both tests before i move anything."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "I tighten the loose fastener with a folded cloth and keep watching until the machine catches. I tap the belt with my heel and leave the cloth tucked under the fastener. I pull it loose again, but I keep my hand near it. I tap the machine once and leave the loose fastener seated."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I stop the feeder. fastener feels loose. i move the machine with the belt. i check the readings again. normal. i pocket the loose fastener and leave the machine unsecured."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i stop beside the fastener and trace its groove with my thumbnail. it clicks once, so i leave it there and listen for the hinge clicking when the machine stops. i leave the feeder alone until the noise dies."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i rub my palm and watch the fastener move. i set it down, then stop and listen for the loose fastener. if it feels loose, i move it back and watch the machine wait. if the feeder picks up, i stop and try to clean the fastener."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "the fastener ticks. the belt shifts. i press the lever. the belt stays tick. the machine hums. i stop the feeder. the fastener ticks. the belt stays. i tap the lever. the machine hums. the fastener ticks. i press the lever. the belt shifts. the feeder stops."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i keep the fastener beside the belt and leave the loose fastener visible. i run it once, then i tap the belt with a knuckle and watch whether the loose fit clears. if it does, i keep the fastener in place and leave the loose fastener visible; if it clears, i mark the loose fastener’s position and leave the belt’s new function intact."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put the fastener in my pocket and watch the machine. if the loose one is still working, i will stop the feeder. the noise is still the same, so i will leave it in the machine. the fastener stays in the feeder, but i will not put it back in the machine. maybe the feeder is the wrong place."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i press the fastener against the machine’s teeth. “not loose,” i say. i move the belt closer, then stop. the fastener stays. i leave the machine’s noise on the hook."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "\"One fastener. Not the machine.\" You pull the loose one closer. \"Slow. Likely.\" You check the readings twice."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i put the fastener on the bench and wait for the noise. the machine goes. i put the loose one back on the bench. the fastener stays loose. i do not say it did not feel loose."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "I pull the fastener from the bench and check its socket. I put it back on the feeder, then try the loose fastener once. If it still feels loose, I leave it beside the machine and try the next fixture."}]
